back: Converging: thicker in the middle, brings parallel rays to a focus. Diverging: thinner in the middle, spreads them out.

front: What is the **principal focus** of a converging lens?
back: The point where rays parallel to the principal axis meet after the lens.
The distance from the centre of the lens to the principal focus.

front: Two rays for a converging-lens diagram?
back: A ray parallel to the axis passes through F; a ray through the centre goes straight on.
Real, inverted, diminished, between F and 2F (camera, eye).
Virtual, upright, enlarged, on the same side as the object (magnifying glass).

front: Lenses for short and long sight?
back: Short sight: diverging lens. Long sight: converging lens.
Real: rays actually meet, can be shown on a screen. Virtual: rays only appear to come from it, cannot be shown on a screen.
